_comment_secrets: C-06: every value below that used to be a real committed secret is now blank. This file is still tracked by git, so nothing that goes here is actually private — fill these in via environment variables (ASP.NET Core's config provider already overrides appsettings.json with environment variables of the same name, using __ as the section separator, e.g. Jwt__PrivateKey, ThaIDConfig__ClientSecret) or a real secret store, never by editing this file directly. Jwt:PrivateKey is this issuer's own access-token signing key — generate a fresh one (the old value was exposed and must be treated as compromised). ThaIDConfig:ClientID/ClientSecret/APIKey are issued by DOPA/Chula and cannot be rotated by this issuer alone — whoever owns that integration must request new credentials from DOPA/Chula, since the old ones were committed to source control and must be considered leaked.

Verifier._comment: PresentationController (OID4VP, per Sequence Diagram - P2 v.1.4.md) uses this to decide whether a presented PID VC's issuer is trusted ("Trust Registry" step) and which vct identifies a PID VC. TrustedPidIssuers is an allowlist of did:web identifiers — start with this issuer's own did:web (self-issued PID VCs, e.g. local/sandbox testing) and add any other trusted PID issuer's did:web once one exists. This is an MVP allowlist, not a real Trust Registry service integration.
